October 4, 2026

Session-wide Qt appearance with restoration

  • Fixed Qt and cursor setup for SDDM sessions using zsh or a separate bash login profile. Appearance exports now cover the active shell and X session startup files, preserving other login setup.
  • Made the Qt appearance page show saved setup status and the selected theme, refreshing immediately after enabling or restoring defaults.
  • Replaced the temporary OpenSnitch relaunch control with generic session-wide Qt setup and desktop activation status. Settings distinguish saved configuration from the current launcher's environment and explain when logout/login is required.
  • Added Restore previous Qt appearance with an original-settings backup retained across theme switches. Restoration preserves unrelated edits, refuses conflicting changes and explains the limits of older setups without backups. Qt setup leaves menu entries and autostart commands untouched; any future launcher edits require an exact-change confirmation and undo.

October 3, 2026

Theme packs, compatibility and reliable browsing

  • Made cursor application consistent for non-GTK apps such as Kitty by publishing Xcursor defaults, X11 resources and cursor launch settings, while preserving unrelated profile, Qt and font settings. Applying a cursor now explains when an app restart is needed.
  • Added Qt application themes through Kvantum on any desktop. Qt appearance settings detect Qt 5/6 plugins, offer repository installation and can enable or remove the session style override. Theme packs include Qt companions; first setup explains the required logout/login.
  • Added a Theme packs category for downloadable bundles that contain usable components for the current desktop. Multi-component installs offer to apply everything, apply the current section or apply later.
  • Expanded compatibility filtering across desktops, window managers and Cinnamon versions. Background archive checks build a local SQLite index with import/export support while cards load immediately.
  • Added smooth card transitions. Off-screen cards wait until they re-enter the viewport before disappearing, preserving the rows currently in view.
  • Remembered scroll positions across launches for browsing, Installed categories and settings. Added uploader profiles with normal theme cards, ratings, pagination and an expanded view.
  • Made large Installed collections load on demand: only the selected category builds cards, and expensive previews and controls wait until a card enters the viewport. Shared compatibility checks across categories and removed repeated full-record reads while building Apply controls. Actions still read fresh records, and bulk selection and saved scroll positions are preserved.
  • Moved archive compatibility scanning out of the app into an independent headless worker with bounded reads, decompression and process memory. Browsing now uses existing local/imported evidence and keeps unknown themes visible. Added portable snapshot generation and explicit HTTPS snapshot imports for future shared hosting.
  • Discarded asynchronous preview callbacks after their GTK widget is destroyed, avoiding updates to cards removed during section changes.
  • Added prompts to install missing dependencies, app update notifications and Update and restart. Fresh Arch/CachyOS sessions can refresh missing package databases after the user agrees to a full system upgrade.
  • Kept rate-limited checks pending without saving incompatibility evidence. One retry queue per host waits through the cooldown and runs checks sequentially; leaving a page cancels waiting checks. Refused download links are refreshed once rather than on every retry.
  • Separated failed requests from genuine empty inspections, bounded Retry-After delays and fixed rate limits hidden inside ZIP errors. Background archive reads fail fast on server errors; cards retain known component information during deferred checks.
  • Formatted the Python codebase and clarified ambiguous sections. Updated installation, update and compatibility documentation.

September 30, 2026

Keep installed themes recorded

  • Fixed installation records being lost when installs or metadata updates overlap. Theme operations and record updates now use thread and process locks.
  • Added durable atomic saves and a previous-version backup. Unreadable records are reported instead of silently replaced, and failed saves preserve existing records.

September 29, 2026

KDE, Xfce and clearer installation progress

  • Added KDE Plasma support and desktop-aware catalog selection, including Plasma styles, global themes, color schemes and Aurorae window borders.
  • Added Xfce appearance controls and panel presets with Undo, along with wallpaper handling and Xfwm previews. Added bulk removal of installed wallpapers and theme packs.
  • Hid unsupported theme sections for the current desktop and window manager. Installation progress now includes downloading, extraction, copying, caching and saving records.
  • Split the GTK interface into focused modules and refreshed the website, README and screenshots.

September 26, 2026

Faster browsing and a clearer view of your desktop

  • Added cached catalog results, smaller previews, background loading and infinite scroll. Fixed hidden tabs starving visible previews and reduced animated-preview CPU use with automatic and hover-only playback.
  • Added an In use view with previews of every active theme component, including themes installed outside Drape. Cards show component glyphs based on archive contents and warn about misplaced uploads.
  • Flagged Cinnamon themes using pre-5.4 dialog styles and warned before applying them. Added a sample window and an optional check showing which open apps use window-manager borders.
  • Added a Window manager settings page with Compiz installation, embedded settings, live package progress and removal of packages Drape installed. Cinnamon gets a separate Compiz login session; MATE and Xfce can switch live.
  • Added replacement of conflicting theme names, including active boot and login themes. Improved the layout for small screens, separated settings in the sidebar and added Drape's application icon.

September 25, 2026

Drape begins

  • Introduced a per-component Linux theme manager backed by GNOME-Look: browse, install and apply icons, cursors, GTK controls, window borders, Cinnamon themes and wallpapers. Added command-line commands and support for catalog install links.
  • Verified downloads, unpacked nested archives, classified theme contents and tracked installs for updates and removal. Added conversion of Windows cursor packs to Linux Xcursor themes and improved download selection.
  • Built the Installed picture grid with category tabs, previews, individual wallpaper removal and an installed-files viewer. Added a variant picker with live previews drawn from theme files.
  • Added boot splash, login screen and lock screen support, including Plymouth, SDDM and LightDM themes. A privileged helper applies system changes with administrator authentication and tracks files Drape owns.
  • Launched the project website, published screenshots and documentation, and added the GPL-3.0 license.
